title: FlowBench: multi-priority token-stream stress lab & regression detector
creator: Jordan Lee
description: Create an extensible end-to-end benchmark (FlowBench) that synthesizes multi-priority token streams across mixed workloads to quantify continuous-batching + queueing interactions and automatically detect p95 regressions versus rolling baselines.
background: Existing synthetic harnesses cover stratified arrival processes and mixed-model sims, but we lack a compact lab that: (1) models multi-priority tenant queues with admission control, (2) emits token-level time-series for batching/queue depth attribution, and (3) runs automated p95 regression checks with alerting. This ticket codifies FlowBench, telem instrumentation, and initial runs against two model profiles.
scope: Deliver bench harness + infra config, instrumentation in runtime probe hooks, dashboard, and a regression detection job. Run baseline experiments and document findings. Do not ship autoscaling policy changes in this ticket; that is follow-up work.
success_criteria: FlowBench repo scaffolded under inference/bench/flowbench with runnable harness script
Telemetry hooks emit tokens_per_sec, batch_occupancy, queue_depth, p95_latency_ms tagged by priority and model_variant
Regression detector job computes rolling-7day median and alerts on >10% p95 increase persistent for 3 runs
Baseline runs for two model profiles completed and recorded in Grafana + Confluence
PR with instrumentation and harness code reviewed and merged
tasks: Design workload taxonomy: control-plane (small text), assistant-chat (multi-turn), rerank (short queries) mapped to priority buckets
Implement arrival generators: poisson, bimodal-bursts, scheduled microbursts
Add per-request priority header and admission control simulator in harness
Instrument runtime probe to sample batch occupancy and queue depth at dequeue events
Hook p95 calculation into regression-detector lambda/job and wire to alerting channel
Create Grafana dashboard panels and Confluence runbook
Run baseline experiments on A100 and H100 nodes and capture results
test_config: mixed_priority.yaml: arrivals: [poisson: lambda=200, microburst: bimodal= {low:50, high:250, p:0.07}], priorities: [high(10%), med(30%), low(60%)], session_lengths: [short:8, medium:64, long:512], model_variants: [rwd-llama-13b-int8, rwd-llama-70b-4bit]
metrics_export: Prometheus endpoint /metrics/flowbench labeled by priority, model, node
experiment_results: Run 2026-03-11 (A100, rwd-llama-13b-int8): tokens_per_sec=18.2k, overall_p95=128ms, high-priority_p95=46ms, batch_occupancy_p95=8
Run 2026-03-12 (H100, rwd-llama-70b-4bit): tokens_per_sec=7.1k, overall_p95=312ms, queue_depth_p95 spiked during microbursts to 42

Observation: small scheduled microbursts amplify tail for low-priority sessions due to pre-emptive admission policy; batch occupancy increased but did not fully explain p95 spikes — queueing contributed ~60% of tail latency
analysis_notes: Trade-off considered: increase max_batch_size to reduce per-token cost vs higher queueing penalty for low-priority work; decided to keep baseline batch limits and explore admission throttle in follow-up
Instrumentation change required minor runtime probe event (dequeue_timestamp) and a light-weight sample exporter; flagged for security review (no PII exported)

We saw non-linear regression when mixing very long sessions (>=1024 tokens) with microbursts; hypothesis: KV cache eviction + re-warming interacts with batching to amplify latency — next_step experiment planned
blockers: Limited H100 capacity in lab week of 2026-03-15 — some runs delayed
Metrics schema change required: prometheus label cardinality must be bounded before enabling per-session_tag export
next_steps: Stabilize regression-detector thresholds: tune from 10% to 8% after 2 more baseline days
Run targeted KV-cache warmup experiments isolating session-length effect
